RunState._drop_disallowed_from_grab_bag (sts2_rl/run.py:769) applies it before EVERY pull and REMOVES the rejects from the bag -- pull_relic_from_front (run.py:731), pull_relic_from_back (run.py:752) and the Shop-rarity bag (run.py:783) are the only three pull paths -- mirroring RelicGrabBag.RemoveDisallowedRelicsFromDeques (RelicGrabBag.cs:218-270), and `Relic.is_allowed_at_neow` now DELEGATES to is_allowed (sts2_rl/relics/base.py:211-222 = RelicModel.cs:443-446) so the Neow pools (sts2_rl/events/neow.py:72) cannot read a stale flag. guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): the sim refuses to OFFER the DIG option when the grab bag is empty; C# always offers it and grants RelicFactory.FallbackRelic instead
guards.issue: MECHANISM: Shovel.TryModifyRestSiteOptions adds `new DigRestSiteOption(player)` unconditionally (Shovel.cs:24) and DigRestSiteOption overrides nothing that could disable it -- RestSiteOption.IsEnabled is the base `=> true` (RestSiteOption.cs:37). If the bag has nothing left, PullFromFront returns null and RelicFactory substitutes FallbackRelic (RelicFactory.cs:47), so the player still gets A relic. shovel.py:18-19 returns early on `not run.has_available_relics()`, so the option does not appear at all; and run.pull_relic_from_front returns None on an empty bag (run.py:585-586), so the sim has no fallback either. Two divergences in one guard: a missing rest-site option, and no fallback relic. DORMANT, and quantified rather than asserted: EXECUTED (relic_probes_b14.py shovel) the bag holds 122 relics at run start and a DIG consumes exactly one (122 -> 121), so emptying it needs ~122 relic acquisitions in a run that offers on the order of 15-20. Porting a relic sink that drains the bag -- or a run length that does -- makes it live; so would any content that empties a single rarity deque, because C#'s GetAvailableDeque then ESCALATES Shop -> Common -> Uncommon -> Rare (RelicGrabBag.cs:227-237) while the sim falls back to `relic_grab_bag.pop(0)` regardless of rarity (run.py:595). That last difference is shared-machinery, not Shovel's, and is reported in the lessons file rather than verdicted here. Rule 7: RestSiteOption.cs, DigRestSiteOption.cs, RelicFactory.cs, RelicGrabBag.cs and run.py are not hashed here.

Checked against PROMPT.md bug class 16's named-stream trap, and this one is wired: shovel.py:21 calls run.obtain_relic_from_grab_bag() with no rarity_rng, and pull_relic_from_front's documented default is `self.rewards_rng` -- the per-player Rewards stream under a parity rng_set and the legacy shared RNG otherwise (run.py:577-595). So the default overload's stream is the one the sim uses. EXECUTED (relic_probes_b14.py shovel): a DIG moves the bag 122 -> 121 and adds a Rare-rolled relic to run.relics. Rule 7: run.py and RelicFactory.cs are not hashed here.

obtain_relic_from_grab_bag pulls and then calls run.add_relic (run.py:631-636), which is the sim's RelicCmd.Obtain -- it fires after_obtained, so a dug Sand Castle or Signet Ring applies its pickup effect exactly as a chest-granted one would. The SharedRelicGrabBag.Remove line is the multiplayer second bag keeping in sync with the per-player one; the sim has a single bag, so the removal has no counterpart to need. Rule 7: run.py is not hashed here.

guards.rationale: Shovel.cs has two members and no fields, so there is no per-combat or per-run counter to reset -- and, unlike Girya, no use limit: the option is offered at every rest site on both sides.
